states.claim: ent1 is the top stack entry obtained from stack; its data zval is owned by ent1 and may be destroyed/freed by this function.
ent1->data is released and then reinitialized as a zend_string zval holding new_str.
fname and retval are local zvals initialized/used for the __wakeup call and then destroyed.
ent2 is the new top stack entry after decrementing stack->top.
target_hash points to the hash table of ent2->data when ent2->data is an array or object.

values.claim: stack->top is decremented by 1 when stack->top > 1, and set to 0 via stack->done=1 otherwise; the decrement is the only index/count update affecting subsequent stack_top accesses.
The base64 decode length argument is Z_STRLEN(ent1->data), the byte length of the string stored in ent1->data.

values.claim: zend_str_tolower is applied in place over exactly Z_STRLEN(ent1->data) bytes of Z_STRVAL(ent1->data), and the resulting Z_STR(ent1->data) is used as the class-table lookup key.
php_store_class_name receives the class-name string pointer and its length Z_STRLEN(ent1->data) from ent1->data.
The key length passed to zend_symtable_str_update is strlen(ent1->varname), the NUL-terminated length of ent1->varname.
When ent1->varname is non-NULL, ent1->data is inserted into target_hash keyed by ent1->varname; when ent1->varname is NULL, ent1->data is appended via zend_hash_next_index_insert.
target_hash is HASH_OF(&ent2->data), so insertions through target_hash alias the hash table of ent2->data.
